purpose: Map capabilities, skills, implementations, agents, hooks, and evidence into fast, evidence-bounded execution routes.

legacy_identity.rule: Legacy names and paths are compatibility identifiers, not the current product brand.

authority.cutover_rule: Current repository remains authoritative until the dedicated repository passes source, build, evidence, consumer, and release-identity parity and the old repository is reduced to an explicit versioned consumer.

compatibility.reason: Avoid breaking launchers, public URLs, storage keys, workflows, and stale/open branch references before dedicated-repository cutover.

release_versioning.scheme_reason: Operant has observable public compatibility boundaries across routes, launcher/acquisition behavior, durable browser state, prompt/capability behavior, and release artifacts. Schema/protocol versions remain independent. Pre-1.0 policy keeps unstable breaking changes within MINOR until an explicit 1.0 compatibility declaration.

bootstrap.rule: Do not rewrite the historical 0.1 identity. The first deterministic release is 0.2.0; after its tag exists, tags are the version-planning baseline.

pre_1_policy.promotion_to_1_0: explicit operator-reviewed compatibility declaration; never inferred from an ordinary commit

release_versioning.rollback: Restore or redeploy a previously tagged commit/artifact. Never decrement, rename, erase, or reuse a released version.
